subject: housing_local_procedure
purpose: Pilot local-procedure overlays for Florida housing and foreclosure. These records describe county/circuit clerk, court, and sheriff procedure; they do not replace statewide substantive law or create statewide deadlines.

sources.agency: Hillsborough County Clerk of Circuit Court & Comptroller
sources.title: Foreclosure Sales
supports: Foreclosure sales are conducted through the Hillsborough Clerk's online sale process; proposed foreclosure judgments/orders and clerk-generated sale/title documents follow the local clerk/court workflow.
This is local operational procedure and does not alter statewide Chapter 45 deadlines.

sources.agency: Hillsborough County Clerk of Circuit Court & Comptroller
sources.title: E-Filing
supports: Hillsborough filing workflows use the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal; issuance and forwarding of writ documents remain separate clerk/sheriff operational steps.

sources.title: Civil Process — Evictions / Writs of Possession
supports: HCSO expressly describes its eviction/writ workflow by reference to Chapter 83 and §83.62 and schedules execution after receiving the writ.
This source does not establish that Chapter 83's eviction-specific 24-hour mechanism governs general foreclosure possession.

sources.title: Circuit Civil
supports: Mortgage foreclosure is handled in Circuit Civil and local case records/dockets are available through the clerk's official systems.

sources.title: Foreclosure Education
supports: Orange Clerk provides foreclosure resources, self-represented e-filing information, and links to online foreclosure sales; these are local information and filing resources.

sources.agency: Ninth Judicial Circuit Court of Florida
sources.title: Foreclosures
supports: Orange County foreclosure cases are handled by the judge assigned to the case and the Ninth Circuit publishes local procedures for foreclosure hearings, continuances, and service-list requirements.
These requirements are local circuit procedure, not statewide substantive foreclosure law.

sources.agency: Ninth Judicial Circuit Court of Florida
sources.title: Civil Case Management
supports: The Ninth Circuit classifies foreclosure as streamlined civil case management and applies its local case-management order/procedures to qualifying cases.
The local case-management framework does not replace statewide response, sale, or possession law.

sources.title: Court Services — Eviction Information
supports: OCSO publishes operational guidance for Chapter 83-style evictions, including a locally described 24-hour writ workflow and sheriff scheduling.
The page's eviction-specific timing must not be generalized to foreclosure possession merely because both use the phrase writ of possession.

sources.title: Foreclosure
supports: Duval Clerk states that an occupied foreclosed property requires a writ of possession rather than purchaser self-help after title, and describes a local 24-hour possession-writ practice.
The local 24-hour statement is clerk informational/operational guidance and is not encoded as a statewide Florida foreclosure deadline.

sources.title: Circuit Civil — Writ of Possession
supports: Duval Clerk states that it issues a writ of possession only when an order or judgment specifically authorizes issuance; clerk issuance is a separate step from sheriff execution.

sources.title: Civil Process — Writ of Possession Procedures
supports: JSO requires a clerk-issued writ and local processing materials, assigns the writ to an officer, and schedules execution operationally based on workload and statutory limits.
JSO says posting may occur the following day or shortly thereafter and expressly describes the page as guidance; the operational schedule is not a fixed statewide legal clock.

sources.title: Residential Foreclosure Division Procedures
supports: The Fourth Circuit's Duval residential-foreclosure procedures, revised June 1, 2026, govern local division designations, communications, hearings, case-management conferences, and proposed-order submission.
These are Duval/Fourth Circuit procedural requirements and not statewide substantive rights or deadlines.

sources.title: Thirteenth Circuit Mortgage Foreclosure Forms
supports: The Thirteenth Circuit currently publishes foreclosure-specific forms including a Uniform Motion for Writ of Possession in Foreclosure Case, confirming a local court-motion/order workflow for post-foreclosure possession.

Because some linked form text predates the current federal PTFA framework, the form index is used only to establish the existence of the local foreclosure-writ motion workflow, not to publish obsolete tenant deadlines.

hillsborough.clerk: Hillsborough County Clerk of Circuit Court & Comptroller

eviction.summary: HCSO's published eviction/writ workflow expressly points to Chapter 83 and §83.62. Keep its residential-eviction mechanics confined to landlord-tenant eviction unless independent foreclosure authority supplies a bridge.

foreclosure.summary: Hillsborough uses Circuit Civil and the Clerk's online judicial-sale workflow. Local filing/sale operations supplement but do not alter Florida's statewide foreclosure event chain. The Thirteenth Circuit also publishes a foreclosure-specific motion-for-writ form; its older tenant-language is not reused as current substantive law.

writ_execution.summary: Sheriff execution is locally scheduled after intake. The available HCSO page is framed around Chapter 83 eviction writs, so it is not used as authority for a general foreclosure-possession countdown.

local_providers.name: Hillsborough County Veteran Community Services / Veterans Resource Center
local_providers.note: County veteran service officers provide free benefits/resource assistance. This is service routing, not foreclosure representation and not a court-deadline extension.

eviction.summary: OCSO publishes an eviction-specific 24-hour writ workflow. It remains an eviction overlay and is not imported into foreclosure possession.

foreclosure.summary: Orange foreclosure cases are routed through the assigned judge and Ninth Circuit case-management/local foreclosure procedures; the Clerk supplies foreclosure education and online-sale routing.

writ_execution.summary: OCSO accepts writs of possession, but its published 24-hour discussion is embedded in eviction guidance. No Orange foreclosure-specific legal countdown is inferred.

local_providers.name: Orange County Veterans Services
local_providers.note: Official county veterans-services office/resource routing. Services vary by program; housing legal representation and eligibility are not guaranteed.

eviction.summary: JSO publishes writ-of-possession processing as local operational guidance. State Chapter 83 eviction law remains separately sourced in the statewide housing dataset.

foreclosure.summary: Duval uses Fourth Circuit residential-foreclosure divisions/procedures and local Clerk sale/title/writ processing. The Clerk states an occupied foreclosed property requires a writ rather than immediate purchaser self-help.

writ_execution.summary: Duval Clerk describes a local 24-hour possession-writ practice after foreclosure, while JSO says actual posting/execution scheduling depends on processing and workload. The 24-hour statement is therefore retained only as local operational guidance, not a statewide legal deadline.

operational_timing.scope: Duval Clerk foreclosure informational guidance only
operational_timing.display: Duval Clerk currently describes a 24-hour local writ-of-possession practice after foreclosure. Treat this as Duval operational guidance; the actual writ, court order, and sheriff process control, and this number is not a statewide Florida foreclosure deadline.

local_providers.name: City of Jacksonville Military Affairs and Veterans Department
local_providers.note: City veteran-service officers and resource routing include benefits, employment/social services, housing/financial-assistance connections, and referrals. Program eligibility and legal representation are not guaranteed.

required_facts: case number or docket if available
router.warning: Never default an unknown county to a pilot county. Local procedures appear only after the user identifies the county or the case papers establish it.

cross_layer_routes.warning: Former owner is not automatically a PTFA tenant.
PTFA applies only if the federal bona fide tenancy conditions are satisfied.
Not PTFA-qualified does not mean no protection; identify lease, foreclosure-party status, judgment, and housing-program overlays.
Unknown occupant status routes to fact identification first and does not assign tenant or former-owner rights.
Local sheriff operations supplement Rule 1.580 but do not create a statewide foreclosure execution deadline.
